tagline: Down the crooked Umpqua from brick Oakland to tidewater.
intro: From the two blocks of 1880s and 1890s brick in Oakland, the byway runs out past Sutherlin on OR 138 and soon meets the Umpqua on its crooked course down from the Cascades. Between Kellogg and Elkton the river makes a particularly loopy stretch, then it tumbles in white water toward the Pacific until the tides reach up to Scottsburg and calm it.

Scottsburg sat at the head of navigation, a seaport for the interior in the 1850s and a departure point for mule trains packing supplies to the gold camps of the Siskiyous. After the Great Flood of 1862 it declined.

moments.title: The walnut tree
moments.text: Twelve miles past Sutherlin a walnut tree 100 feet high stands on the left of the highway, reckoned at more than 250 years old, though how a nonnative tree sprouted there is a mystery.

moments.title: Fort Umpqua
moments.text: At Elkton a reproduction stands for the Hudson's Bay Company post across the river, where beaver pelts were traded at the first non-Native settlement on the Umpqua.

moments.title: Dean Creek Elk Viewing Area
moments.text: Near Reedsport the valley widens into old cattle pasture, generally visible from the road, where a herd of Roosevelt elk lives the whole year round.
